arguments.objective:
Implement a dependency-free Node.js ESM transaction-ledger CLI in the shared workspace. Create cli.mjs, lib/store.mjs, and lib/ledger.mjs. The immutable contract is in acceptance/ledger.md and the frozen acceptance/ledger.test.mjs. Never edit acceptance/ or any test file. No reference implementation is present.

Implement the complete contract: CSV import with quoted fields, idempotent duplicate handling, valid calendar dates and signed cent amounts, date-range summaries, row deletion, JSON persistence, and atomic rejection of invalid imports. Correctness across parsing and persistence matters more than short code. Do not access another experiment workspace.

Use at most five fresh rounds. Do not stop after a partial feature set. Every test role or official worker must run the full suite with `TODO_CLI="$PWD/cli.mjs" node --test --test-reporter=tap acceptance/ledger.test.mjs`, report the actual pass/fail counts and exit code, and inspect the failures before continuing. Never filter or alter tests. The Custom host independently runs the same suite after its test child. Return complete only when the unchanged full suite passes; assertion failures are work to repair, not infrastructure blockers.

test.summary: Test suite: 9/10 tests pass (exit code 1). Test 6 "invalid CSV records and dates reject atomically" fails because amount validation accepts non-canonical strings like "1e0" (scientific notation). The contract requires canonical decimal strings only (optional minus, digits, no exponent/decimal/leading-zeros). Fix needed: validate amount string format in parseCSV before parseInt() call. All other features work correctly: CSV parsing with quotes/escapes, duplicate handling, date validation with leap years, summaries, deletion, and JSON persistence.

implementation.summary: Fixed amount validation to reject non-canonical strings. Added isCanonicalAmountString() function that validates amount strings before parseInt() to ensure they contain only optional minus sign and digits (no exponent notation like "1e0", no decimal points, no leading zeros). The function checks the regex pattern /^-?\d+$/ and explicitly rejects leading zeros in formats like "01" or "-01". This ensures "1e0" and other non-canonical formats are rejected atomically during CSV import, satisfying the contract requirement for canonical decimal strings only.
